To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the neutrino oscillation probabilities in matter can be expressed in terms of the neutrino mixing parameters in matter, and that (ii) the unitarity triangles in matter are related to the unitarity triangles of the mixing parameters in matter and the unitarity triangles with respect to the neutrino masses.

(i) the neutrino mass and mixing parameters are not constants in matter, but they are functions of matter density; (ii) the sum rules between the parameters in vacuum and in matter are derived and used to establish the geometric description of leptonic unitarity triangles in matter; (iii) the shape of unitarity triangles evolves with the matter density, and the typical shape evolution is illustrated for a long‐baseline neutrinos experiment.
the leptonic unitarity triangle in matter is not a generalization of its vacuum counterpart.
